rv.q: It is a humane and, in the final scene, touching vision. But it is also one that is slow in coming.
At times it feels as if two different plays have been pushed together, but, with Ayckbourn, it’s inevitable that we get an unexpected twist at the end.
It is, above all, another cracking good show from the master craftsman.

cn.t: Ayckbourn's 91st play earns positive notices for its timely exploration of mistrust and conspiracy culture in the modern age. Critics praise the sharp social commentary and unexpected twists that keep audiences engaged throughout.
